proofs.statement_en_llm: ExceptT is the error monad transformer: it wraps a monad m so that computations can also fail with an error of type e. This theorem says that if you take an ordinary m-computation x and lift it into ExceptT e m, then unwrap it again with .run, you get back exactly x with its result tagged as a success (Except.ok <$> x). In short: lifting adds an error channel but never uses it.
proofs.proof_sketch_en_llm: The proof is a single rfl. ExceptT e m a is defined to literally BE m (Except e a), .run is the identity function, and the MonadLift instance for ExceptT is defined as fmapping Except.ok over the computation, so both sides of the equation unfold to the same term with no reasoning steps at all.

proofs.statement_en_llm: Take two lists whose elements are themselves lists. If l1 is a sublist of l2 (obtained by deleting some entries while keeping the order of the rest), then concatenating all of l1's inner lists yields a sublist of the concatenation of l2's inner lists. candidates.name: Measurable
candidates.explanation_llm: Measurable is the predicate that preimages of measurable sets are measurable. It is the side condition needed for the pushforward-composition lemma to apply.

candidates.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.map_map
candidates.explanation_llm: MeasureTheory.Measure.map_map is the functoriality lemma for pushforward: for measurable g and f, pushing forward along f and then along g equals pushing forward along g after f. This is the mathematical heart of the proof.

proofs.statement_en_llm: Let A be a C*-algebra without a unit, and embed an element x into its unitization (A with a complex unit adjoined). The theorem says x's image lies in the order interval from 0 to 1 exactly when x is a positive element and its norm is at most 1. This version states the norm bound using the nonnegative-real-valued norm rather than the ordinary real norm.
proofs.proof_sketch_en_llm: The nonnegative-real norm is the same number as the ordinary norm, just carried in a type where nonnegativity is built in, so the inequality 'norm at most 1' is the same proposition in both phrasings. The proof therefore just cites the real-norm version of the lemma directly, with no rewriting needed.

candidates.name: NonUnitalRing.toNonUnitalSemiring
candidates.explanation_llm: NonUnitalRing.toNonUnitalSemiring is the forgetful instance that drops subtraction and negation, viewing a non-unital ring as a non-unital semiring. It is needed only because the star-ordered-ring axiom is stated over semirings. Typeclass plumbing.

candidates.name: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra
candidates.explanation_llm: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra is the class of complex C*-algebras with no unit element: a complete normed non-unital algebra over the complex numbers with an involution satisfying the C*-identity (norm of star-a times a equals the square of the norm of a). It is the ambient setting of the theorem.

candidates.name: PartialOrder
candidates.explanation_llm: PartialOrder is the reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric less-or-equal relation. Here it is the order on the C*-algebra that makes the interval from 0 to 1 meaningful.

candidates.name: StarOrderedRing
candidates.explanation_llm: StarOrderedRing is the axiom tying the order to the involution: x is at most y precisely when y minus x is a sum of elements of the form star-s times s. It is what makes '0 <= x' mean 'x is a positive element' in the operator-algebra sense.

candidates.name: NonUnitalNormedRing.toNonUnitalRing
candidates.explanation_llm: NonUnitalNormedRing.toNonUnitalRing is the forgetful instance extracting the bare ring structure from a normed non-unital ring, discarding the norm. Typeclass plumbing on the path from the C*-algebra class down to the order axioms.

candidates.name: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra.toStarRing
candidates.explanation_llm: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra.toStarRing is the projection supplying the involution (the star operation) together with its compatibility with addition and multiplication. It is one of the ingredients StarOrderedRing needs.

candidates.name: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra.toNonUnitalNormedRing
candidates.explanation_llm: NonUnitalCStarAlgebra.toNonUnitalNormedRing is the projection supplying the norm and the underlying non-unital ring structure out of the C*-algebra bundle. Typeclass plumbing.

candidates.name: CStarAlgebra.inr_mem_Icc_iff_norm_le
candidates.explanation_llm: CStarAlgebra.inr_mem_Icc_iff_norm_le is precisely this statement with the ordinary real-valued norm. It is the entire proof; its own justification uses that the embedding into the unitization is isometric and that a positive element has norm at most 1 exactly when it is bounded above by the unit.

global_score_caveat: score_pct is the candidate's position in this ranking's GLOBAL score order over the whole universe, ties sharing a percentile. Cross-proof score comparability has never been validated in this program: a key that orders candidates correctly within a proof need not be comparable between proofs. Treat the global-threshold policy as exploratory.
